changes.subject: basketball
changes.anchor: Box Score and Shooting Percentages From Your Games
changes.why: Learners (and the app's own gates) must not read meaning into ten shots. Computed: Wilson 95% intervals 7/10 = 0.40-0.89 and 5/10 = 0.24-0.76 overlap; a 60% shooter makes 7 of 10 about 21% of the time and 5 of 10 about 20%. Supports the honest combine gates and the 'own baseline' rule.
changes.staged_line: [Analytics] Log Fifty Shots Before Judging a Change | Log fifty attempts over several days before deciding a change worked, because 7 of 10 and 5 of 10 can come from one shooter.
changes.line: [Analytics] Log Fifty Shots Before Judging a Change | Log fifty attempts over several days before deciding a change worked, because 7 of 10 and 5 of 10 can come from one shooter.
changes.minimax_draft: [Analytics] Log Fifty Shots Before Judging a Change | Log at least 50 attempts over several days before deciding whether a shot change worked, because 10-shot ranges overlap while 50 attempts narrow the uncertainty.
claims: With 10 attempts, the 95% ranges around 7 of 10 and 5 of 10 overlap.
At 50 attempts, the 95% margin for a 70% shooter is about 13 percentage points either way.

judged.line: [Analytics] Log Fifty Shots Before Judging a Change | Log fifty attempts over several days before deciding a change worked, because 7 of 10 and 5 of 10 can come from one shooter.

judge_a.issue: The evidence shows that ten-shot results are too uncertain, but it does not establish that exactly fifty shots are sufficient to decide that a change worked. The example also provides no baseline or decision criterion beyond collecting more shots.
judge_a.better: [Analytics] Log Fifty Shots Before Judging a Change | Log at least 50 attempts over several days before deciding whether a shot change worked, because 10-shot ranges overlap while 50 attempts narrow the uncertainty.

changes.subject: basketball
changes.anchor: Short Daily Sessions Beat One Long Cram
changes.why: Contextual interference: blocked practice scores best during practice, varied practice retains and transfers better (Shamshiri et al. 2025 in novices' jump shots; increasing-schedule RCT). The app's gates already use the day-2 cold set; this lesson tells the learner why.
changes.staged_line: [Practice] Judge Shooting by the Next-Day Cold Set | Take ten elbow jump shots the next day before shooting from the elbow again, because a block of the same shot inflates today's percentage.
changes.line: [Practice] Judge Shooting by the Next-Day Cold Set | Take ten elbow jump shots the next day before shooting from the elbow again, because a block of the same shot inflates today's percentage.
changes.minimax_draft: [Practice] Judge Shooting by the Next-Day Cold Set | After the general warm-up, log your first ten elbow jump shots before taking any other elbow shots, because same-shot repetition can make today’s percentage look better than next-day retention.
claims: Blocked same-shot practice gives the best scores during practice, while varied or random practice gives better retention and transfer (Shamshiri et al. 2025).
Log the first ten shots from the spot the next day as the cold score.

judged.line: [Practice] Judge Shooting by the Next-Day Cold Set | Take ten elbow jump shots the next day before shooting from the elbow again, because a block of the same shot inflates today's percentage.

judge_a.issue: The instruction is internally ambiguous because it tells the learner to take elbow jump shots before shooting from the elbow again. It also mischaracterizes blocked practice as inherently inflating a percentage; it produces higher immediate, task-specific scores that need not represent retention or transfer.
judge_a.better: [Practice] Judge Shooting by the Next-Day Cold Set | After the general warm-up, log your first ten elbow jump shots before taking any other elbow shots, because same-shot repetition can make today's percentage look better than next-day retention.

changes.subject: piano
changes.anchor: Shape One Practice Session From Warm-Up to Review
changes.why: Learners' own judgement of learning points the wrong way: random-order melody practice retained better at two days while learners predicted the reverse (Abushanab and Bishara 2013); benefit holds for short units once learned (Verwey et al. 2021). The live path only teaches interleaving explicitly at P09 ('Interleaving and Spacing Pieces Across the Week'), though [Mixed] rounds already interleave from P04.
changes.staged_line: [Practice] Shuffle Short Units Once Each Plays Correctly | Shuffle your G, D, F and A major scales once each plays correctly, because mixed practice feels harder but your next-day cold take improves.
changes.line: [Practice] Shuffle Short Units Once Each Plays Correctly | Shuffle your G, D, F and A major scales once each plays correctly, because mixed practice feels harder but your next-day cold take improves.
changes.minimax_draft: [Practice] Shuffle Scales After One Correct Run | Play G, D, F and A major scales correctly once each, then shuffle their order, because random-order practice is retained better two days later even though it feels harder.
claims: Shuffle only after each short unit has had one correct run.
Random-order practice of short melodies was retained better two days later than fixed-order practice, while learners judged the opposite (Abushanab and Bishara 2013).

judged.line: [Practice] Shuffle Short Units Once Each Plays Correctly | Shuffle your G, D, F and A major scales once each plays correctly, because mixed practice feels harder but your next-day cold take improves.

judge_a.issue: The cited retention finding concerns two days, not a guaranteed improvement on a next-day cold test. The wording also does not clearly say to shuffle the order of the scales, which is the mixed-practice manipulation supported by the evidence.
judge_a.better: [Practice] Shuffle Scales After One Correct Run | Play G, D, F and A major scales correctly once each, then shuffle their order, because random-order practice is retained better two days later even though it feels harder.

judge_b.issue: The line claims “next‑day cold take improves,” but the cited evidence (Abushanab & Bishara 2013; Verwey et al. 2021) only shows better retention at two days, not the next day.
judge_b.better: [Practice] Shuffle Short Units Once Each Plays Correctly | Shuffle your G, D, F and A major scales once each, because mixed practice feels harder but retention improves after two days.
